quest.village-quest.daily.honey.title: The Queen's Gift
quest.village-quest.daily.honey.offer.1:
This year's bloom was so rich that my hives are overflowing - honey is already dripping from the combs!
If nobody helps soon, the bees will run out of room and leave.
quest.village-quest.daily.honey.offer.2: After accepting, use Glass Bottles on full Bee Nests or Beehives to collect honey. Use Shears to harvest honeycombs. Each counter shows the required number of harvests.
quest.village-quest.daily.honey.completi: The yard smells like summer again, and the bees dance as if it had never been any other way.
You saved more than you know - thank you, friend.
You’ve earned these coins. And I suspect you’ll smell of honey for a while yet!
quest.village-quest.daily.pet_collar.tit: A New Collar for a Faithful Friend
quest.village-quest.daily.pet_collar.off: Has your companion’s collar seen better days? A little dye could give it a fresh look.
After accepting, use dye to change your tamed wolf’s or cat’s collar colour until the objective counter is full. You can recolour the same animal more than once; each colour change uses dye.
quest.village-quest.daily.pet_collar.com: The color shines, and your faithful companion wears it with pride.
Such care travels fast - thank you for your effort.
Here are a few coins in thanks for your handiwork.
quest.village-quest.daily.wheat.title: Bakehouse Help
quest.village-quest.daily.wheat.offer.1: The bakehouse is short on both grain and finished loaves, and morning will come fast.
quest.village-quest.daily.wheat.offer.2: After accepting, harvest ripe wheat for the displayed wheat delivery and extra for the bread. Then craft the bread yourself. Bring the full amount of wheat and the bread to the Questmaster; both are consumed at hand-in.
quest.village-quest.daily.wheat.stage.3: Stage 3 · Deliver wheat and bread to the Questmaster
quest.village-quest.daily.wheat.completi: The sacks are filled, and the smell of fresh bread finally returns to the bakehouse.
A village eats well when someone sees the work through from field to oven.
Take a few coins in thanks for your effort.
quest.village-quest.daily.potato.title: Kitchen Supplies
quest.village-quest.daily.potato.offer.1: The pots are waiting in the village kitchen, but potatoes and carrots are running low. Supper needs a bit of both.
quest.village-quest.daily.potato.offer.2: After accepting, harvest ripe Potato and Carrot crops and collect their drops. The objective counters show the required amounts.
quest.village-quest.daily.potato.complet: A good harvest for the village kitchen. There will be a proper supper again.
Anyone who keeps both fields moving saves a village from many thin meals.
Here, take some coins for the road.
quest.village-quest.daily.wood.title: Fuel for the Workshop
quest.village-quest.daily.wood.offer.1: The workshop needs timber, and the furnace needs fuel. Without both, work comes to a halt.
quest.village-quest.daily.wood.offer.2: Chop the required logs and collect freshly mined coal after accepting. Dropped player items and charcoal do not count; keep the materials.
quest.village-quest.daily.wood.completio: Timber is cut and coal is mined. Thank you for your work — that is a good start.
Timber for the workbench, coal for the fire — you have put in a good day’s work.
Take these coins in thanks for your work.
quest.village-quest.daily.coal.title: A Favor for the Smithy
quest.village-quest.daily.coal.offer.1: The smithy needs ore for metal and coal for heat - one without the other is only half a day's work.
quest.village-quest.daily.coal.offer.2: After accepting, mine the required raw iron and coal yourself. Carry the full ore-and-coal bundle to the Questmaster; it will be consumed at hand-in.
quest.village-quest.daily.coal.completio: The furnace is glowing, the ore is ready, and honest work rings through the smithy again.
With ore and coal delivered, the smithy can carry on working.
Take these coins as your pay.
quest.village-quest.daily.wool.title: Wool for the Weaver
quest.village-quest.daily.wool.offer.1: The weaver is waiting for fresh wool. Before the loom can clatter again, the sheep need shearing.
quest.village-quest.daily.wool.offer.2: After accepting, shear Sheep. The objective counter shows how many to shear. You do not need to hand in wool.
quest.village-quest.daily.wool.completio: The sheep are sheared. Thank you for taking that work off the weaver’s hands.
The sheep are cared for, and the weaver has plenty to work with.
Here are coins in thanks for your trouble.
quest.village-quest.daily.river.title: Meal from the River
quest.village-quest.daily.river.offer.1: Fish are biting down by the river, but the kitchen will stay quiet until someone brings in the catch.
quest.village-quest.daily.river.offer.2: After accepting, first catch the required fish with a fishing rod. Then take cooked cod or cooked salmon from a furnace and bring the required amount to the Questmaster. It is consumed at hand-in.
quest.village-quest.daily.river.stage.2: Stage 2 · Take cooked fish from a furnace: %s/%s
quest.village-quest.daily.river.stage.3: Stage 3 · Hand in cooked cod or salmon to the Questmaster
quest.village-quest.daily.river.completi: The catch is in, and the smell of a proper riverside meal finally drifts from the kitchen.
You caught and cooked the fish yourself. That makes for a proper meal.
Take a few coins for your work.
quest.village-quest.daily.autumn.title: Autumn Harvest
quest.village-quest.daily.autumn.offer.1: The pumpkins and melons are ripe. If we wait too long, part of the harvest will be left in the fields.
quest.village-quest.daily.autumn.offer.2: After accepting, harvest Pumpkin and Melon blocks. Each block counts once; Melon Slices do not count separately.
quest.village-quest.daily.autumn.complet: The pumpkins and melons are harvested. Thank you for helping in the fields in time.
You did not merely collect produce - you saved the harvest at the right time.
Here are coins for you and your timely help.
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.title: Smelting for the Smithy
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.offer.1: The forge is burning, but without fresh iron the anvils will fall silent.
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.offer.2: After accepting, first collect the required raw iron. Then take the required iron ingots from a furnace and hand them in to the Questmaster. The delivered amount is consumed.
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.stage.2: Stage 2 · Take iron ingots from a furnace: %s/%s
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.stage.3: Stage 3 · Hand in raw iron and iron ingots to the Questmaster
quest.village-quest.daily.smelt.completi: The ore is mined, the ingots are stacked, and proper work rings through the smithy again.
Raw iron has become ingots. Now the smith can put them to good use.
Take these coins in thanks for your work.
quest.village-quest.daily.stall.title: New Life in the Stable
quest.village-quest.daily.stall.offer.1: The stable has grown quiet. A few young animals would bring life back to the farm.
quest.village-quest.daily.stall.offer.2: After accepting, breed animals: feed suitable adult pairs and let them produce offspring. The objective counter shows the required breeding events.
quest.village-quest.daily.stall.completi: There is movement in the stable again, and the promise of new life finally hangs over the pens.
Care with livestock always pays twice - today that is easy to see.
Here are coins for your help.
quest.village-quest.daily.trade.title: Business in the Village
quest.village-quest.daily.trade.offer.1: The stalls are ready, but few goods are changing hands. Help get market day moving.
quest.village-quest.daily.trade.offer.2: After accepting, trade with villagers. Sell goods to earn the required Emeralds. The objectives show both targets.
quest.village-quest.daily.trade.completi: The trade crates are changing hands again, and the village market finally feels alive.
Good trade fills more than purses – it keeps the storerooms supplied.
Take these coins in thanks for your help at the market.
quest.village-quest.special.shards.title: Whispers of the Shards
quest.village-quest.special.shards.offer: Ten Magic Shards whisper softly in your pack. Bring them to me, and I will open a hidden trial of magic.

The %s Magic Shards are consumed when you accept. Then mine 16 Amethyst Shards yourself. Brew 3 potions and take them from the brewing stand. Enchant 1 item at an enchanting table or anvil. Obtain 1 Ender Pearl and 1 Blaze Rod from your own loot; a delivered Pilgrim material reward also counts for the Blaze Rod. Return to the Questmaster for the treasure map.
quest.village-quest.special.shards.cache: The map's red X points toward a buried cache in the Overworld.
Unearth the chest beneath the marked spot and open it to recover your Starreach Ring. Do not break the chest itself.
quest.village-quest.special.shards.map_g: You have passed the trial. I have marked a hidden cache on this map.
Follow the red X, unearth the chest and open it. Your Starreach Ring is waiting inside.
quest.village-quest.special.shards.map_r: Here is the map to your cache again. Follow the red X and unearth the chest beneath it.
quest.village-quest.special.shards.compl: The Starreach Ring answers your hand at last, and the old shard-song falls quiet.
Carry the ring in your offhand. It lets you reach two blocks farther when building.
quest.village-quest.special.merchant.off: Your name is known along the trade roads. Now you can prove your skill with merchants and wares – and earn the Merchant’s Seal.

After accepting, complete 20 villager trades and earn 128 emeralds through them. Make 10 purchases of goods from villagers and 2 purchases from a Pilgrim. Then return to the Questmaster for your seal; no goods need to be handed in.
quest.village-quest.special.merchant.com: The Merchant’s Seal is yours now. May it serve you well on the trade roads.
While sneaking, right-click a Pilgrim or wandering trader with the seal to refresh their wares. You can do this once in total per daily quest cycle.
quest.village-quest.special.flute.title: Shepherd's Flute
You know how to tend a herd. But the Shepherd’s Flute answers only to someone even timid creatures can trust.
After accepting, breed animals to produce 20 offspring. Also tame a wolf, a cat and a parrot. Then return to the Questmaster to claim the flute.
quest.village-quest.special.flute.comple: The Shepherd's Flute now answers your breath, and even skittish creatures listen to its call.
Right-click with the flute to call animals within 24 blocks towards you. While sneaking, its call briefly stops them.

screen.village-quest.journal.summary.sto: Every deed in this village is recorded in its archives. Whoever crosses the paths of its people writes themselves into the chronicle. This journal bears witness to you.
screen.village-quest.journal.commands.in: Here you’ll find the most useful commands for quests and everyday village life.

screen.village-quest.journal.commands.qu: Call the Questmaster near you to offer or review quests.

screen.village-quest.journal.flow.2: Review the offer in the Questmaster board and accept it there, or use /vq daily accept while a chat offer is open.

screen.village-quest.journal.flow.5: You can review active quest progress here at any time and cancel the current daily or weekly with the red X.
screen.village-quest.journal.flow.6: When the ledger asks for crafted or forged proof, only fresh work made during the active quest counts. Old village stock from a chest does not.
The village remembers every steady hand. Each completed task strengthens your standing with the people who live and work here.

screen.village-quest.journal.relics.surv: Sneak-right-click to change the destination. Right-click normally to point the needle towards it. For Home, right-click twice within 10 seconds: you return to a safe place at your valid respawn point, or the world spawn as a fallback. Home then recharges for 30 minutes of server running time. Biome and structure searches have a 30-second cooldown, even if nothing is found. Later, the Questmaster and a Pilgrim can unlock more destinations.
screen.village-quest.journal.help.1: There are daily quests that can be completed anew each day.
screen.village-quest.journal.help.2: The server sets the daily reset. It can follow real time or Overworld Minecraft days. The Questmaster shows the time remaining.
screen.village-quest.journal.help.3: For chat offers, click one of the choices shown in the message. You can also accept an open daily offer with /vq daily accept.
screen.village-quest.journal.help.4: In the journal you can manage quests, check progress, and cancel them.

quest.village-quest.weekly.harvest.offer: Winter will not wait for our granary to fill. Let’s gather enough supplies while we can.

quest.village-quest.weekly.pasture.offer: Healthy herds are the village's quiet wealth.

After accepting, breed animals, shear sheep and collect the required wool. Breeding counts when offspring are produced. Hand in the wool to the Questmaster; it will be consumed. The three objective counters show the required amounts.
quest.village-quest.weekly.pasture.compl: The barns are lively and the wool baskets finally look full.
The Questmaster notes that the herds have been well kept.
quest.village-quest.weekly.market.title: Market Week
A proper market week brings silver, emeralds, and word from the road.
After accepting, trade with villagers and earn Emeralds from them. Also buy goods from the Pilgrim. Follow all three objective counters.
quest.village-quest.weekly.market.comple: The stalls were busy. Coins, goods and news passed from hand to hand.

quest.village-quest.weekly.nightwatch.of: The nights have grown restless around the village paths.

quest.village-quest.weekly.nightwatch.co: The roads are quiet again, and lanterns shine late into the night.

quest.village-quest.weekly.roadwarden.of: Traders and pilgrims have begun to avoid the road since monsters appeared. Make the way safe again.

quest.village-quest.weekly.roadwarden.co: The road signs still stand, and the path is safer for every traveler.

quest.village-quest.daily.spider_sweep.o: Fresh webs keep appearing around barns, fences, and the low orchard walls.

quest.village-quest.daily.spider_sweep.c: There is less scuttling around the barns and fences. The yard feels a little more peaceful.

quest.village-quest.special.apiarist_smo: Our hives are thriving, but good tending needs more than one careful pair of hands.

quest.village-quest.story.failing_harves: The Failing Harvest
Barren Fields
The wheat is growing thin, and supplies are running low. If we are to avoid a failed harvest, we must start in the fields.
After accepting, harvest 16 wheat and 8 potatoes from ripe crops. Bring both to the Questmaster; the supplies are consumed from your inventory at hand-in.
Wheat: %s/%s | Potatoes: %s/%s
Fresh grain and potatoes fill the first gaps in the storehouse.
It is not abundance yet, but it is enough to quiet the first worry.
The Questmaster thanks you. The village has enough to get through the next few days.
Quiet Hives
The hives should have carried some of the burden, yet even the apiary has gone strangely quiet.
Deliver 3 Honey Bottles and 1 Honeycomb to the Questmaster. Supplies from full hives, storage, trade or other sources all count. They are consumed at hand-in.
Honey Bottles: %s/%s | Honeycomb: %s/%s
Honey and wax are back in the storehouse, easing the beekeepers’ immediate worries.
The comb will provide wax, and the honey will stretch the dwindling supplies.
The Questmaster gratefully accepts the delivery.
Bread For The Square
Fields and hives may promise relief, but people believe only when the square smells like food again.
After accepting, craft 6 bread and take 4 baked potatoes from a furnace output. Bring both to the Questmaster; all 10 food items are consumed from your inventory at hand-in.
Bread: %s/%s | Baked Potatoes: %s/%s
Warm bread returns to the square, and even the worried voices grow less sharp around the stalls.
A warm meal gives people hope again.
There is enough food on the square for today. Tomorrow, the work will continue.
Market Relief
The supplies will last for now. The traders need customers again if the village is to get back on its feet.
After accepting, complete at least 2 villager trades and earn 4 emeralds in total from trading. Help bring life back to the market.
Trades: %s/%s | Emeralds: %s/%s
Trade returns to the market, and the fear of a failed harvest begins to fade.
Your work has earned more than thanks. The village trusts you and sees you as part of its future.
The Apiary Charter is now entered into the village ledger in your name.
A good market day begins with people talking. Make a round of the village, hear from the traders and help a few deals along.
After accepting, right-click 10 different adult villagers with professions to speak with them, and complete 5 trades with villagers.
You have spoken with the traders and brought some life back to the market.
A good market thrives on its goods and on the people who meet there.
Take wages for your market round.
screen.village-quest.questmaster.story.s: The forge burns cleanly again, the hall is provisioned, and the Forge Charter now carries your name.
screen.village-quest.questmaster.story.m: Trade has returned to the market road, and the Market Charter now bears your name.

message.village-quest.story.market_road_: By evening, prices are being called again and shutters are lifting. The market lives. Return to the Questmaster.

quest.village-quest.project.watch_bell.d: The village night watch has been reset around your work, and every alarm now carries more weight.

quest.village-quest.project.watch_bell.m: Since it was raised, the night watch sounds like a duty people trust, and word now reaches you sooner when the road edge turns dangerous.

After accepting the contract, take your Wayfinder into a village, a Pillager Outpost, a Woodland Mansion and a Swamp Hut in the Overworld. Right-click it inside each structure without sneaking to record its roadmark. Return to the Pilgrim with your valid compass; it is not consumed.

quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.que: “When skeletons lurk along the roads, few people dare carry a lantern outside,” says the Pilgrim. “Help us make the nights safer.”

Thank you for keeping watch. Those who travel late will be grateful.

quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.woo: “A fire brings little comfort when every shadow might be a creeper,” says the Pilgrim. “Our travellers need quieter nights.”
After accepting, defeat creepers in the Overworld at night. Your objective shows the required number. Then return to the Pilgrim.
“A few fewer creepers, a few quieter nights,” says the Pilgrim. “Well done.”
The travellers can give more thought to their fires and less to every shadow.
Pilgrim contract complete: Smoke Beyond the Milestone.
quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.tra: “Once the moon rises, you can hear zombies shuffling over the gravel,” says the Pilgrim. “No wonder some carters wait until morning.”
After accepting, defeat zombies in the Overworld at night. Your objective shows the required number. Then return to the Pilgrim.
The Pilgrim listens to your report. “Good. Each zombie gone is one less worry for the late carters.”
Thank you for venturing out after dark.
Pilgrim contract complete: Tracks in the Dark.
quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.fan: “You often notice webs in the grass only when you are caught in them,” says the Pilgrim. “That keeps many travellers off the field roads at night.”
After accepting, defeat spiders in the Overworld at night. Your objective shows the required number. Then return to the Pilgrim.
“You have dealt with the spiders. That helps everyone travelling on foot,” says the Pilgrim.
Work like this draws little attention, but travellers appreciate it all the same.
Pilgrim contract complete: Fangs by the Hedgerow.
quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.ash: “The Nether has enough bad roads already,” says the Pilgrim. “Blazes and wither skeletons make every journey harder. Can you deal with some of them?”
After accepting, defeat blazes and wither skeletons in the Nether. Your objectives show the required numbers. Then return to the Pilgrim.
The Pilgrim nods as you tell him about the blazes and wither skeletons you defeated. “I am glad you made it back safely.”
The Nether remains dangerous. Your help makes the journey a little easier.
Pilgrim contract complete: Ash on the Pass.
quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.smo: “Magma cubes leap into your path while ghasts shriek overhead,” says the Pilgrim. “In the Nether, even a good road is seldom enough.”
After accepting, defeat magma cubes and ghasts in the Nether. Your objectives show the required numbers. Then return to the Pilgrim.
“You faced the magma cubes and ghasts and made it back,” says the Pilgrim. “That is no small task.”
Thank you for your help. I will tell the other travellers about it.
Pilgrim contract complete: Smoke over Blackstone.
quest.village-quest.pilgrim.contract.sti: “Few return from the End with good news,” the Pilgrim says quietly. “Endermen and shulkers wait there. I need someone who can face them.”
After accepting, defeat endermen and shulkers in the End. Your objectives show the required numbers. Then return to the Pilgrim.
The Pilgrim listens carefully as you describe your hunt in the End. “It is good to see you back here.”
You have fulfilled the contract. May your next distant journey bring you safely home as well.
Pilgrim contract complete: Stillness beyond the Gate.
quest.village-quest.story.silent_forge.c: Cold Hearth
The forge is not only quiet, it is hollow. Without ore, coal, and a few rarer finds, nobody will believe this hall is ready to make honest work again.
After accepting, mine and collect 64 Coal, 40 Raw Iron, 24 Redstone Dust, 16 Raw Gold and 4 Diamonds. Deliver these amounts to the Questmaster for the forge stores; they are consumed at hand-in.
Coal: %s/%s
Raw Iron: %s/%s
Redstone: %s/%s
Raw Gold: %s/%s

The first supplies have reached the forge. The quiet hall can become a workshop again.
Coal, metal and diamonds are ready. The smiths can begin preparing their work.
The Questmaster draws the first line beneath the reopening of the forge.
The Bellows Breathe Again
The forge needs more than a fire. With blast furnaces and cauldrons, the smiths can work the metal and get back to their craft.

After accepting, take 24 iron ingots from furnace outputs. Deliver 24 iron ingots, 3 Blast Furnaces and 3 Cauldrons to the Questmaster; all are consumed at hand-in. The furnaces and cauldrons may come from storage or trade.
Iron Ingots: %s/%s
Blast Furnace: %s/%s | Cauldron: %s/%s
Blast furnaces and cauldrons are ready for the forge. The new iron supplies will get work moving again.
The smiths once again have what they need to make good tools.
The Questmaster writes the forge back into the ledger as working space.
Tools For The Hall
An open furnace without tools is only hot air. The hall needs pieces that prove useful work can come out of it again.
After accepting, craft 1 Iron Pickaxe, 1 Bucket, 1 pair of Shears and 1 Shield. Deliver all four to the Questmaster undamaged. All are consumed.
Pickaxe: %s/%s | Bucket: %s/%s
Shears: %s/%s | Shield: %s/%s
The new tools are ready: carefully made and still unused.
The village can put them to work building, tending its supplies and keeping people safe.
The Questmaster marks the forge as able to supply the village again.

Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection and Projectile Protection all count. Any level is valid. Already enchanted equipment is accepted. The five equipment pieces are consumed at hand-in. You keep the books.

The Master's Edge
Good equipment also needs the librarians’ knowledge. After accepting, buy an enchanted book with Sharpness and an enchanted book with a protection enchantment from villagers.
Bring the Questmaster a Diamond Sword with Sharpness. Also deliver an Iron Helmet, Iron Chestplate, Iron Leggings and Iron Boots, each with a protection enchantment.

The hall has fire, tools, and knowledge again. The final equipment set is complete as well.
What began as a silent forge can now serve the village again.

quest.village-quest.story.market_road_tr: Market Road Troubles
Shuttered Stalls
The market road is short of customers. Traders wait for business while the village grows worried about the market.
After accepting, earn 64 emeralds by trading with villagers. It will help bring the first market stalls back to life.
Emeralds: %s/%s
Coin is visibly moving from hand to hand again.
Where emeralds flow honestly, certain fears go quiet faster than promises ever could.
The first traders are pleased. Your business has brought life back to the market.
Ledger And Notices
The traders need paper and books for price lists, notices and ledgers. Help them keep a proper record of their business again.
After accepting, craft 96 Paper and 16 Books. You may bind books before finishing all the paper. Deliver 48 Paper and all 16 Books to the Questmaster; the delivery is consumed.
Paper Crafted: %s/%s | Books Crafted: %s/%s
Stage 1 · Craft Paper: %s/%s
Stage 2 · Craft Books: %s/%s
Bring 48 Paper and 16 Books to the Questmaster
Paper and books return to the market, and with them comes accountability.
A village trusts a price more easily once it can be written down.
The Questmaster sets the market ledgers in order once more.
Goods Must Flow
Order alone does not open a stall. People must see goods truly moving up and down the road again.
After accepting, make 24 trades with villagers. Also speak with adult villagers from 4 different working professions of your choice. Unemployed villagers and nitwits do not count.
Trades: %s/%s
Working professions contacted: %s/%s
The stalls have customers again, and goods are changing hands among the traders.
People can see that a trip to the market is worthwhile again.
The Questmaster records that the road is moving properly again.
Market Day Returns
The traders are ready. Speak to the villagers and invite them to the market. Once enough people are near the bell, market day can begin.
After accepting, speak with 6 different adult villagers. Then ring a bell with at least 6 adult villagers nearby, within 20 blocks in each direction from the bell block.
Villagers spoken to: %s/%s
Bell Rings: %s/%s
People are bargaining and laughing at the market again. The worries of recent days are easing.
The market road now carries voices, prices, and confidence at the same time again.
The Market Charter is now entered into the village ledger in your name.
Restless Pens
Empty Troughs
Feed is running low, and there is plenty of work around the pens. Help the herders stock up and raise new animals.
After accepting, breed animals to produce 12 offspring and deliver 48 Hay Bales to the Questmaster. The Hay Bales are consumed at hand-in.
Animal births: %s/%s
Hay Bales: %s/%s
The pens are lively again, and the herders look over the fence with renewed contentment.
A stable feels healthier the moment feed and young stock can be seen together again.
With feed in store and young animals in the herd, the herders can breathe more easily.
Wool Before Weather
The next cold wind will come soon enough. The herders need help with the shearing so the village has wool to spare.
After accepting, shear 24 sheep and carry 48 wool of any color to the Questmaster. The wool delivery will be consumed at hand-in.
Sheared Sheep: %s/%s
Wool: %s/%s
The wool bundles rise again, and the pasture no longer looks like work left undone.
With this wool in store, the village can face the cold evenings with less worry.
The Questmaster accepts the wool. The village is ready for the next cold spell.
New Pastures
The herd is supplied. Now it is time to look beyond the village fence: take a horse and explore the roads and pastures nearby.
After accepting, ride 2,400 blocks on horseback to scout new pastures and possible trade routes.
Horseback Distance: %s/%s
The country has been sounded out under hoof instead of guessed at from the gate.
A village grows stronger when its keepers know where the next pasture and road might lie.
The Questmaster records that the village is looking outward again.
The Shepherd's Call
A dependable herder knows the herd and prepares for the next ride. Gather the animals by the bell and have horse armor ready.

Ring a bell with at least 8 pasture animals nearby, within 12 blocks in each direction from the bell block. Young animals count too. Also carry any Minecraft horse armor in your inventory; you keep it.
Herd called together: %s/%s
Herd called together: %s/%s
Horse Armor ready: %s/%s
The bell rings over the gathered herd. The herders’ work has paid off.
The herders have feed, wool and a well-tended herd again. The village can count on them.
The Pasture Charter is now entered into the village ledger in your name.

message.village-quest.story.restless_pen: The voices around the pens are speaking with each other again instead of against each other. Return to the Questmaster.

quest.village-quest.story.night_bells.ch: First Watch
People can only sleep soundly when someone is guarding the village. Tonight, the paths must be made safe again.
After accepting, defeat a total of 7 zombies at night so the people living by the roads can sleep more easily.
Zombies defeated at night: %s/%s
Protection prep: bell: %s/%s | watch sectors: %s/%s | supplies: %s/%s
The first shadows fall back, and the heavy unease around the houses falls with them.
Tonight, people can sleep a little more easily.
The Questmaster thanks you for keeping watch along the roads.
Drive Back the Dark
If skeletons hold the lanes and spiders take the outer fields, nobody will keep faith in safe paths between house, field, and pen.
After accepting, defeat a total of 5 skeletons and 3 spiders at night to make travel between the houses and fields safer.
Defeated at night: %s/%s skeletons | %s/%s spiders
Perimeter prep: bell: %s/%s | protected sectors: %s/%s | supplies: %s/%s
The road belongs to the village again, not the shapes that wait at its edge.
Fewer shadows mean more courage for everyone who must step out first in the morning.
The Questmaster is relieved to hear that you have guarded the roads.
Hold The Road
The night watch needs someone who can stand firm when several dangers lurk along the roads. Watch for creepers and other hostile creatures.
After accepting, defeat a total of 11 hostile creatures at night, including at least 3 creepers. You may complete the task over several nights.
Defeated at night: %s/%s creepers | %s/%s hostiles total
Route emergency: bell: %s/%s | route markers: %s/%s | provisions: %s/%s
The night still tests the village, but it no longer slips through unopposed.
Whoever holds the road-edge often holds together the courage of the whole village.
Your watch has given the village confidence. The Questmaster thanks you.
Morning After The Alarm
The true proof of a watch is not a single swing, but whether the village can stand through a whole assault and still greet morning together.
After accepting, survive a raid in victory and gain the Hero of the Village effect. Then return to the Questmaster. If the effect is already active when you accept, it must expire first.
Successful Raids: %s/%s
Full defense: bell: %s/%s | sectors: %s/%s | equipment: %s/%s (golem and final confirmation also required)
Your last victory still lingers. Wait for Hero of the Village to expire, then win a new raid.
Finish every protection step and bring the listed supplies before reporting back.

quest.village-quest.story.night_bells.ch: Morning does not arrive in exhausted silence, but in loud relief.
A village that survives a raid remembers for a long time who stood at its bell.
The Watch Bell is now entered into the village ledger in your name.
A sealed warning for the trade guild.
screen.village-quest.questmaster.story.s: Help the Pilgrim resolve three combat rumors. Then the guild will need your help on the trade road. %1$s/%2$s
The trade road stands open again, and the guild remembers who held the line.
quest.village-quest.story.shadows_on_the: Shadows on the Trade Road
Whispers Between Bells
Too many traders leave with good wares and never return. Before anyone rides blind into the dark, the village wants names, rumors, and hard details.

After accepting, speak with 6 different adults in the home village and 2 different adults in each of 4 other inhabited villages. The village where you first speak to someone becomes the home village for this task.
Home village accounts: %s/%s
Other villages questioned: %s/%s
Question %s different adults in each other village
People in every village describe the same danger. These are no longer mere rumors.
The road is not merely unsafe. Someone is hunting it with intent.
The Questmaster records enough testimony to act on the danger.
A Needle for the Night Road
If the caravans carry shard-charged ledgers and sealed trade stock, the Wayfinder's Compass can be tuned to their distress trails.
Carry your Wayfinder's Compass and speak to a toolsmith so it can be aligned for the night road.
Compass calibrated: %s/%s
The toolsmith sets the compass against the pull of shard-stock and caravan iron.
From now on, the road can call for help instead of merely swallowing the missing.
Your compass can now follow the caravans’ distress calls.
First Signal
The first distress trail will be the test. Reach the caravan at night and keep the merchants standing through the attack.
Wait for night and follow the Caravan Distress marker with your compass. Defeat every attack wave; at least one merchant must survive. Then return to the Questmaster.
The first rescue breaks the easy confidence of the raiders.
The merchants have seen someone fight to bring them home safely.
The Questmaster receives your report on the rescued caravan.
Holding the Trade Road
One caravan is safe, but more traders are still on the road. Keep the route clear and help them return safely too.
Answer two more nighttime Caravan Distress calls. Defeat every wave at each caravan; at least one merchant must survive each encounter.
The attacks grow harsher, but the road no longer belongs entirely to the raiders.
Survivors now carry more than fear back with them. They carry proof.
A battered merchant asks for one last audience before the matter reaches the guild.
A Letter for the Guild
One of the surviving merchants has ridden in with a sealed warning for the guild. The letter must reach the Questmaster intact.
Speak to the courier and bring his sealed Guild Warning Letter to the Questmaster. The letter is handed over and removed from your inventory at turn-in.
Speak to the surviving guild courier.
Bring the sealed guild warning to the Questmaster.
Letter secured: %s/%s
The warning reaches trusted hands before the raiders can choose the hour for themselves.
The guild responds quickly: a larger convoy is about to set out and needs your protection.
The Questmaster starts counting down the nights until the guild convoy rides.
Bell Over the Trade Road
In two nights, a heavily laden guild convoy will set out. The raiders are unlikely to pass up the chance. Prepare for a major attack.
On the announced night, follow the Guild Convoy marker with your compass. Defeat every wave and keep at least one merchant alive.
Great convoy secured: %s/%s
Nights remaining until the convoy moves: %s
The raiders hit with everything they had, and still the convoy stood.
Trade will travel again not because the dark vanished, but because it was met and beaten back.
The Questmaster enters the reopened road into the village record under your watch.
Successful rescues: %s/%s
Current wave: %s/%s
Route emergency: checkpoints: %s/%s | supplies delivered: %s/%s
Enemies remaining %s
Caravan survivors: %s/%s
No call for help has arrived yet. Stay ready for the next caravan.
The caravan travels at night. Wait for darkness, then follow the compass.
The distress trail is live. Follow the compass and reach the caravan.
message.village-quest.story.shadows_on_t: You can only hear these rumors in a village. Go there and ask the locals.
You need your Wayfinder’s Compass before you can accept this task.
Good. I will tune the needle to shard freight and caravan iron. Choose Caravan Distress on your compass. When a caravan needs help at night, it will lead you there.
The courier presses a sealed warning letter into your hand. The guild must hear of this before another escort sets out.
Take the letter back to the Questmaster before the next convoy takes the road.
Take the letter to the Questmaster soon. The guild must know what is happening on the road.
Bring the sealed Guild Warning Letter to the Questmaster to finish the task.
The compass has located the caravan. Follow its route marker.
The first roadside position was obstructed. The compass has locked onto a nearby safe caravan site.
No safe caravan site could be prepared here. Move to more open terrain and try again.
The guild convoy has arrived. Follow its route marker.
You handed %s bread to the caravan.
The caravan was lost. Another distress trail will surface on the next night.
The guild convoy did not make it through. The guild will try again the next night.
The caravan survives and the road carries witnesses home.
The great convoy holds. The road is yours tonight.
A guild merchant is waiting with a sealed message.
message.village-quest.dialogue.market_ro: So long as trade lives in the market, the village heart beats the steadier for it.
Good to see someone still making the rounds instead of cowering behind shut doors.
Keep the stalls lively, and the road will seem far less forsaken.
A busy market leaves less room for worried whispers.
When the bell rings and the square fills, the traders will take heart again.
A crowded market day settles more hearts than any ledger ever could.
When the square feels alive again, even the trade road seems less threatening.
The more voices gather by the bell, the fewer whispers speak of a dying market.
If caravans cease to come, the iron goes cold and every order behind it begins to stall.
Hope alone will not keep traders safe. They need sound equipment and a clear road to the market.
A village lives by its fields, but it thrives by what it can still send beyond its bounds.
When the roads fall silent, even a fine catch feels as though it will spoil where it lies.
Wool stacked to the rafters is of little use if no caravan dares the road.
Closed roads cost more than coin. They fray the bonds between villages.
message.village-quest.dialogue.shadows_h: Two salt traders rode out before first light, and not so much as a single mule came home.
Last night I heard bells upon the road, and then nothing but silence. It is the silence that troubles me.
They say the missing caravans carried shard wares. If that is true, these raids were no work of chance.
More wagons leave than ever return now. Even the ledgers tell the tale.
Someone watches the trade road with patience and chooses the dark by design.
When three villages tell the same story, it is no longer a rumor but a warning.
message.village-quest.dialogue.shadows_r: No, nothing certain. Only word of yet another cart lost after moonrise.
My cousin rode with dyed wool three nights ago. Only the mule found its way back.
The richest caravans are struck first. Someone is choosing prey, not meeting it by chance.
We bar our doors earlier with each passing night. No trade village should be made to live so.
They strike after dark, always where the road broadens and weary travelers think to rest awhile.
One survivor swore he saw armed raiders driving the monsters straight onto the wagons.
If the guild is not warned soon, the next great convoy will ride headlong into a trap.
We heard steel, then cries, then nothing at all. And that silence keeps returning.

quest.village-quest.story.the_empty_cara: The Empty Caravan
The Cart That Returned Alone
An empty cart has returned to the village. There is no sign of its driver or its sealed cargo.
Choose Empty caravan on your Wayfinder’s Compass and follow the trail. Approach within 10 blocks of the marked resting place to investigate it.
Abandoned caravan investigated: %s/%s
The cart is empty, but its silence is staged rather than natural.
Mud was brushed from one side, harness leather cut from the other, and the guild seal pressed twice.
Someone wanted the village to see a robbery and stop asking who arranged it.
Three Broken Signs
The false trail leaves three small mistakes: a reversed mile mark, wax beneath a wheel rut, and a courier's knot tied by the wrong hand.
Use your Wayfinder’s Compass to follow the three clues in order. Approach within 7 blocks of each marker; the next target appears after you inspect it.
Road signs investigated: %s/%s
Each sign points away from common bandits and toward someone who knows guild procedure.
The same counterfeit seal touched all three sites.
Ink and wax may now name the hand behind it.
Ink Beneath the Wax
The Questmaster can reveal the hidden impression. He needs paper, ink and wax from honeycomb.
Bring 12 paper, 3 ink sacs, and 2 honeycomb to reconstruct the forged seal. These are supplies, so stored or traded goods are valid; the bundle is consumed.
Paper: %s/%s
Ink sacs: %s/%s
Honeycomb: %s/%s
The second impression reveals a merchant house struck from the guild rolls years ago.
Its old routes are being used to move coerced traders under borrowed names.
Three witnesses from the village can tell true names from false ones.
Names Behind the Seal
A cartographer knows the roads, a librarian knows the records, and a cleric knows the families who vanished from them.
Question one adult villager of each profession and join their testimony.
Distinct witnesses heard: %s/%s
The witnesses separate the ringleaders from merchants forced to carry their mark.
That distinction gives the village a choice no patrol usually offers.
A bait caravan can draw the forged guild into the open.
The Bait Caravan

How should the guild proceed? Right-click the Questmaster while holding any banner to offer amnesty to the coerced traders. Hold an iron sword instead to demand a strict judgment. You keep the item; your choice applies to this attempt.
Then follow the Empty caravan marker with your Wayfinder’s Compass. Defeat all attackers drawn to the bait and return to the Questmaster.

quest.village-quest.story.shrines_betwee: Stones That Remember
Use the Cartographer’s Lens in %s different villages connected by your trade routes.
Every road begins in a place with its own needs.
You have learned what makes the villages along your routes distinct.
The Lens is now fitted into your Caravan Ledger.
You can now use the Ledger along the way to see what those villages need.
The Broken Heartstone
The Lens set into your Ledger has traced a distant blue resonance onto an old trail map.
Follow the red mark on the trail map. Once the ruin appears, break its carved milestone to recover the Cracked Shrine Core.
The Cracked Shrine Core has been recovered from the ruin.
A trace of its old power remains beneath the weathered stone.
Perhaps the guild’s craftspeople know how to restore it.
Three Hands of the Guild
After accepting, speak with a Cartographer, a Toolsmith and a Cleric.
Deliver 16 Amethyst Shards, 8 Gold Ingots, 16 Lapis Lazuli and the Cracked Shrine Core to the Questmaster. These supplies are consumed. You receive the Restored Shrine Core.

The cracked core and your supplies have become a Restored Shrine Core.
It can now become the heart of a new Wayshrine.
The First Flame
Build your first Guild Wayshrine and awaken it with the Wayfarer’s Sigil. Your Homestead is a good place to begin.
Life stirs within the restored core. Hold the Wayfarer’s Sigil in your main hand and right-click the placed shrine without sneaking.

Earn at least Trusted standing in two villages and expand your network to three bound Wayshrines in total.
Local requests turn destinations into allies.
Two villages have placed their trust in you.
Three Wayshrines now belong to your network.
More familiar places now await you on your travels.
The Last Relay
Deliver a new guild freight shipment. Where caravans travel the roads, also help them through a new incident.

Only freight arrivals and resolved incidents after accepting count. If an incident is still needed, one begins at the next suitable point near the route’s midpoint. When caravans are shown only on the map, the new freight arrival is enough.

A Table for Everyone
A village needs a place where its people can gather and be heard. I will mark the Council Seat recipe in your book. Craft one and give the council a place of its own.

Give the council a roof, a table, 2 extra stair chairs, books and light. Open the Council Seat and follow its building checks. In an existing village, complete 2 local delivery requests at its Guild Notice Post to earn the residents’ trust (Trusted standing), then accept the mandate at the seat. You may instead begin an empty settlement of your own. Name the village, establish its council and choose it as your Story target before returning to me.
The council now has a place. Its name will endure even if you move one day.
The inn barrel, market desk and storehouse anchor are unlocked. Build them in your own order.
The next steps belong to the same village. A second village will not take its place.
Three Open Doors
The council has its table. Now our neighbours need a warm inn, a lively market and a dependable storehouse. Your next recipes are the Inn Barrel, Market Desk and Storehouse Anchor.

Give each place a suitable building, open its anchor and follow the checklist for this same village. At the market, add a Trader Stall with its own chest or barrel beside it and room to stand in front, then assign it at the Market Desk. Bring me word when the three places are ready. Already confirmed buildings in this village count too, even if a friend built them. Choose the same village as your story target at its Council Seat; you need village management rights to select it yourself.
All three doors are open. The buildings belong together without having to look alike.
Your building work is recognized. A provisional trade route and the Caravan Ledger are now available; the larger Caravan Yard remains a separate later goal.
Now we should learn the names and voices behind those doors.
The Faces of Our Village
Stone walls alone do not make a village. Meet the speaker by the council, the innkeeper at the inn and the storekeeper at the storehouse. Hear what each has to say.

Speak to all 3 in our chosen village, then return to me. Keep their buildings open and valid; if someone is sleeping, visit by day. An empty or abandoned settlement needs 3 adult villagers with assigned reachable beds and time to recover while you stay nearby. The Journal's Villages page shows its condition.
Now the buildings have voices. We know the people we can rely on.
Their names and histories belong to our village.
Next, let us turn good intentions into real help.
What Actually Arrives
Let us put the new market to use. Buy or sell something with a visiting trader in our village; a fair exchange will give these empty counters a purpose.

Also complete a freight contract on an Overworld route connected to this village. The Caravan Ledger’s map guide explains the road; /vq routes contracts shows the trade guild’s offers and how to load them. The next arrival completes supplied freight. The storekeeper can tell you about deliveries but does not issue contracts. Return when trade and freight are done.
The goods arrived and the payment is right. This is how reliability grows.
At the market and storehouse, your promise has become help people can use.
Now we can build something that helps our village for the long term.
A Shared Beginning

Our village has people, trade and a road that carries more than promises. Let the council put its first shared work into the record: open Village projects at the Council Seat and read what is still needed.

Meet the project's remaining needs. In the village area, 3 adult villagers need their own assigned reachable beds; at least one must have a job and be able to reach its claimed workstation. When the council's requirements are complete, choose Recognize project. Return to me for the Village Seal. This recognition will remain part of the village's story.
This improvement belongs to everyone who lives here. Our village has taken its first shared step.
The Village Seal helps you inspect nearby loaded buildings and their condition. If it is lost, the Guild Archive can replace it.
No ceremony is needed. Go out and see what our village needs next.

message.village-quest.kingdom.crisis_voi: We asked for %3$s, not a miracle. I know %1$s has people to feed too. Hear us both before you promise; I would rather keep an honest neighbour than a grand speech.
You kept your supplies. That was hard for us, but I want to hear how it came to that. Come back and speak with me.
We have both said what hurt. Now I want us at one table again: a new meeting, with the same people and no borrowed promises.
We can put this matter behind us. If new difficulties arise, we will sit down together again. Our door remains open.
This opportunity has passed. I do not know your reasons and will not guess at them. We can talk when help is needed again.
Our report lists %3$s. Before we argue about loyalties, speak to both villages and look at what can actually arrive.
The promise was paused by a decision, not bad weather. I can respect a difficult choice. I need you to stand behind it before we build another agreement.
We need word that the shortage has eased – or a new delivery of the needed goods. Then speak with both of us again.
The dispute is settled. The deliveries remain recorded in the village ledger. Good news alone does not make someone a hero.
This opportunity closed without a decision against us. I will record that plainly. Guesswork belongs in neither the pantry nor the minutes.
We need %3$s. Better to promise less and keep your word than offer more than you can deliver. Hear both sides, then decide.
I remember your withdrawal. I will not pretend it was merely a delayed wagon. If we speak again, start with that truth.
Let us both speak, and show me a working direct route. I am not asking for another tribute. I am asking whether the next promise can reach us.
We have a basis to speak again. A repaired understanding is a beginning; the next agreement still needs both signatures.
Silence is not betrayal. The deadline has passed, but our agreement still stands. I will wait for news.
Our request is %3$s. My cupboard has declined to negotiate with empty words. Fortunately, I still will: hear both villages, then make a promise with wheels.
The supplies stayed with you. That hurt us. My good quill is still ready if an honest talk brings us to a new agreement.
Come to a new meeting. No grand banner, no wagon of apology cakes; just both of us, the truth, and enough patience to hear it.
A difficult page, but not a torn-out one. We have finished this mediation. Let the next promise earn its own ink.
The moment passed. I have many talents; reading guilt into a missing conversation is not one of them. We can leave this without blame.
%2$s has asked for %3$s. Our own people matter too. Hear their leader, hear me, and make a choice you can explain to both tables.
We kept our supplies home. That choice has a reason and a cost. Go hear the other leader before you call it a misunderstanding.
Tell both sides the truth again. Repair the reason for the mistrust; a routine trade is not an apology.
This mediation is over. Any goods that actually arrived remain in the village ledger. We will discuss the next agreement together.
The opportunity has passed. Our promise still stands; I will not blame you for putting off an answer.

quest.village-quest.story.artifact_journ: The Unwritten Promise

Finish Bells of Concord and A Place at the Table, and earn all nine permanent guild tools plus the Village Seal. Lost tools can be recovered from the Guild Archive; borrowed or Creative items do not grant entry.

Choose a village whose council you may represent. Near its confirmed Council Seat, use /vq artifacts target, then return to the Questmaster. Your village from “A Place at the Table” is used initially if it is still available.
Our promise concerns: %s
Compass set to %s (%s, %s). This is a recorded place, not a report of its present condition.
The council has recorded your destination. Completed chapters are kept; you must repeat the tasks in the current chapter.
[Choose this village · reset current chapter tasks]
You need one clearly identified, currently checked Council Seat nearby and permission to represent its village. Choosing a charter also requires both tasks in the final chapter to be complete.

Both keep all reward choices, grant the same title and reduce the Village Seal cooldown to three seconds. Change the charter later at this council; no second reward.

[Keep the road open]

Open-road charter recorded. Every promised delivery will name both its sender and its recipient.

The storekeeper adds a shelf label: “Promised is not packed.” The speaker signs beneath it. Your reserve charter remains in this journal; /vq artifacts road can amend it at the same council without another reward.

The speaker rewrites the margin as a proper delivery record. The storekeeper supplies the final correction: “Legible names, please.” Your open-road charter remains in this journal; /vq artifacts reserve can amend it at the same council without another reward.

A road without a recipient
The Questmaster finds only one line in the Concord register: “Supplies will follow.” To the speaker it is a promise; to the storekeeper, an overdue delivery. But no one signed it.
Before anyone is blamed, follow the clues. Your tools know pieces of the same story: the village, the road and the place where the delivery was expected.

Choose a village registered as the destination of one of your active village-to-village routes. Use the Wayfinder’s Compass without sneaking to point it there. At the destination, sneak-use the upgraded Caravan Ledger and use the Wayfarer’s Sigil to inspect a bound Wayshrine or a point within 8 blocks of your route. The Ledger and Sigil checks must be within 96 blocks of the village’s recorded arrival point.
The road existed. The recipient did not exist on paper.
The storekeeper has kept an empty shelf for a shipment nobody actually dispatched.
Find out what can honestly be supplied before writing another promise.
What the map cannot count
“There is a farm on the map,” says the speaker. “A map never fed a sheep,” replies the storekeeper. The farm is real; its work still has to be done.
Lead an animal to a safe place on the farm and tend a hive until it produces honey again. Use your own farm or one agreed with the locals; there is no need to damage anything.

Use the Shepherd’s Flute without sneaking with an animal 6 to 24 blocks away. Within 30 seconds it must move at least 4 blocks and come within 3 blocks of you, on solid dry ground, out of water and not burning. Also use the Apiarist’s Smoker to fill a Bee Nest or Beehive whose honey level is below full. Both deeds must succeed within 96 blocks of the destination village’s recorded arrival point.
The first useful supplies were never missing from a caravan. They were waiting for ordinary care.
The village speaker crosses out “available” and writes “ready for work” instead.
Now make the handover point as reliable as the supplies.
The lever above the door
An old note reads, “Signal when ready.” The lever is high enough to keep children from pulling it. Unfortunately, most adults cannot reach it either.

Check a working building with the Village Seal. Also toggle a signal lever that you can reach only with the Starreach Ring’s extra range. A building that already meets the requirements counts; nothing needs to be damaged.

Keep the Starreach Ring in your offhand. Without Creative mode, toggle a permitted lever beyond your normal block reach but within its 2-block extension. Use the Village Seal to check an officially confirmed building in the destination village with a current valid building report. The lever and building must be within 96 blocks of the village’s recorded arrival point.
The signal works, and the building behind it works too.
The storekeeper attaches a second note: “A green light means ready. It does not mean somebody has already loaded the wagon.”
There is still an unsigned line between an offer and a delivery.
The other side of the seal
A trader recognises the phrase from an old offer: “Supplies will follow the road.” The speaker copied the first three words. The storekeeper never saw the rest.

Nobody stole the goods. Along the way, a travel note became a promise of delivery. Use the Merchant’s Seal to see a different offer. Then pack all the cargo for a contract bound for the waiting village in the Guild Courier’s Satchel and see that the same shipment arrives.

While sneaking, use the Merchant’s Seal to change a pilgrim’s or wandering trader’s offer. Accept a guild freight contract on an active direct route to the destination village. During this chapter, fill the Guild Courier’s Satchel with all its contract cargo, supply that same contract and await its arrival. You may pack at the sending village. A different or reaccepted contract cannot replace this proof. There is no second freight reward.
This time a named shipment reaches a named recipient.
The empty shelf finally earns its label. The speaker asks to keep the faulty note as a reminder; the storekeeper agrees, provided it is filed under “not a contract.”
Decide what your next promise should protect first.
A name beneath the promise
The road is usable and the storehouse is no longer waiting on a rumor. One question remains: should the first promise protect a local reserve, or keep supplies moving between places?
A promise takes more than fine words. Watch a journey along the road, use the Horn to guard it or find a danger, then sign the charter you can stand behind.

Use the Roadwarden Horn within 96 blocks of the destination village’s recorded arrival point. Arm it or, if already used today, have it point out an active route incident. Await a new arrival on an active direct route to the village. Once both tasks are complete, choose a charter near its valid Council Seat with /vq artifacts reserve or /vq artifacts road. You need permission to represent the village. You can change the choice there later without another reward.
The Concord register gains a proper signature and a promise with a clear meaning.
Your old tools have worked together, and every one returns with you. Choose the large building, road or coin package in the reward panel.
No ceremony follows. The next wagon has a destination, and the people waiting for it know who made the promise.
I wrote “supplies will follow.” I thought the rest was understood. That may be the least useful sentence I have ever written.
I kept that shelf empty for weeks. Very tidy. Entirely useless.
The farm was on my map. I forgot that somebody still has to walk out there.
Bring care, not another estimate. A calm animal and a working hive tell me more than a full page of numbers.
The high lever is meant to signal readiness. Please use an agreed one; this misunderstanding needs no broken doors.

screen.village-quest.setup.cooldown.help: On keeps the normal one-hour real-time wait between story arcs. Off skips only this wait. It does not bypass story prerequisites or repeat rewards; saved deadlines are preserved.
screen.village-quest.setup.caravans.help: Full uses normal physical caravan presentation. Reduced limits the physical representation. Map only uses map markers instead of interactive caravan bodies; some physical encounters are unavailable. Routes, cargo and earned progress remain saved.

quest.village-quest.friends.title: Travelling Friends
quest.village-quest.friends.visit_guest: Accept and hand in with the visiting quest giver at the inn. Progress remains while they are away.
quest.village-quest.friends.completed: Thank you, my friend. You have completed the task.
quest.village-quest.friends.not_ready: The task or materials are still incomplete, or your reward queue is full.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.1.dial: Most travellers watch only the road. The most interesting things grow beside it. Bring me some plants; even the ordinary has its secrets.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.1.obje: Bring Simon 8 dandelions, 8 poppies and 8 ferns. The plants are consumed at turn-in. Use Shears to gather ferns.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.1.rewa: 10 Silvermarks; 1.5 experience bars; 3 Potions of Swiftness II (1:30)
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.2.titl: A Thousand Steps, a Thousand Stories
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.2.dial: A map shows where the world ends. Your feet show what lies between. Go out and return with a story.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.2.obje: Travel 20,000 blocks on foot after accepting. Walking, sprinting and sneaking count; riding, flight and teleportation do not.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.2.rewa: 30 Silvermarks; 4 experience bars; Wayfarer’s Token (Speed II for 30 seconds)
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.3.dial: A stranger may be a friend whose story you have not heard. In every village someone has a tale to tell. Listen.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.3.obje: After accepting, speak with residents in 3 different villages across at least 2 biomes.
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.3.rewa: 25 Silvermarks; 4 experience bars; 3 golden Weather Tonics (20 minutes)
quest.village-quest.friends.simon.again: Good to see you again! The roadside herbs always remind me of our travels.
My herb pouch is empty again. Bring me 8 dandelions, 8 poppies and 8 ferns, and I will trade them for 1 Weather Tonic. The plants are consumed.
quest.village-quest.friends.weather.unav: Use this in the Overworld when no Weather Tonic is active.
quest.village-quest.friends.weather.used: The Overworld’s weather has changed for at least 20 minutes of server running time.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.1.dial: I crossed an ocean with more maps than clean shirts. Help me learn these lands before I draw another crooked coast.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.1.obje: After accepting, discover 3 different surface biomes in the Overworld. Oceans and rivers do not count.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.2.dial: My friends will follow the coast. Three lights will tell them they have reached friendly shores. I will mark the places for you.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.2.obje: Build 3 coastal signals at Lutte’s map targets and keep them intact until turn-in.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.2.rewa: 20 Silvermarks; 3 experience bars; Unbreaking III enchanted book
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.3.dial: Some materials are too precious for mistakes. Fortunately, I have already made mine. Bring what I need, and choose your masterpiece.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.3.obje: Complete The Silent Forge. Bring Lutte 2 Ancient Debris, 16 Redstone Dust and 8 Amethyst Shards; they are consumed. On first completion, then choose exactly one tool from your pending rewards.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.3.rewa: Netherite pickaxe: Efficiency IV, Unbreaking III; OR netherite sword: Sharpness IV, Unbreaking III
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.again: My friend! If you ever cross the ocean, follow the lights home.
item.village-quest.weather_tonic.lore: Drink to change the weather across the Overworld for 20 minutes of server running time. Consumes the tonic; usable only when no Weather Tonic is active.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.replac: Missing your valid chart from your inventory? I can draw a replacement: 3 paper, 1 ink sac and 2 Minecraft days. Old copies will be superseded; building supplies are not replaced.
Another lost chart? From the third replacement: 3 paper, 1 ink sac, 5 diamonds and 14 Minecraft days. Old copies will be superseded; no new building supplies.

quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.wait: I am still drawing! Come back after %s more Minecraft day(s).
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.lost: You scatterbrain! Two weeks I spent on that chart, and you lost it between breakfast and sunset. This time I am writing your name on it. Come back in two Minecraft days.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.vacati: Again?! I crossed an ocean and survived storms, and now I draw your lost charts for a living! Five diamonds for my nerves. Then fourteen days of holiday. No charts. No coasts. No you.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.collec: Here. Extra-thick paper this time. Perhaps I can find the next one when the wind carries it off.
quest.village-quest.friends.lutte.forge_: First complete The Silent Forge. Make room in your pending rewards before accepting the masterpiece.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.1.dia: A quiet village means a busy watch. Deal with fifteen monsters near a village at night. I will take the first shift. On paper.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.1.obj: After accepting, defeat 15 monsters near a village in the Overworld at night.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.2.dia: Our iron colleagues work every shift. Their holiday requests are still on my desk. Until approval, repair fifty missing health points across any iron golems with iron ingots.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.2.obj: After accepting, restore a total of 50 missing HP to iron golems using Iron Ingots. Player-built golems and locations outside villages also count.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.3.dia: We need someone who stays when things get serious. Accept, then tell me when you are ready. We will prepare the watch for the next nightfall. The level I raid will only begin once you are back here at night.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.3.obj: After accepting, tell Marius you are ready and return to this host village at the next nightfall. Defeat at least 3 raiders yourself and win that same level I raid.
quest.village-quest.friends.marius.again: The village sleeps better with you on watch. My colleague is still waiting for his holiday approval.

command.village-quest.personal_reset.war: This restarts your own Village Quest progress: both story slots, quests, reputation, village links, routes and VQ money. You leave your party and guild. VQ items are removed from your inventory and Ender Chest, including portable containers, cursor and crafting slots. Ordinary Minecraft items, placed world objects and shared village rights stay. Your old personal tools stored elsewhere become invalid. Other players and earned shared-project claims are preserved. Collect outstanding rewards and settle deliveries first. Reward caps and previous payouts stay recorded; replaying does not pay them again. Close containers and leave room for all cursor, crafting and rescued contents.
